review_response.finding: DE-0011 removed in every scenario (rf_link has no credential), so the compromised-keys clause is not modelled; RD-0003.02 and REC-0003.04 orphaned.
review_response.action: fixed: rf_link now carries credential mission_valid with credential_quote 'malicious use of compromised master keys or any encryption key', so the engine adds a keyed scenario in which DE-0011 is accepted and its preparation rows have a step.

review_response.finding: DE-0011 coded as evasion although ENISA says nothing about hiding.
review_response.action: fixed: role execution with a role_reason (key use is the attack; ENISA claims no concealment). Kept as the best SPARTA wording for use of a valid credential; no entry or execution technique fits better.

review_response.finding: EX-0006 turns a passive interception threat into a command to disable encryption.
review_response.action: kept because ENISA's 'exploitation of weak communications protocols' can be a downgrade (null ciphers, fallbacks, unencrypted service requested with a key), and nine other threats drop to TR45 for it. Changed: it is no longer a precondition of the interception (EXF-0003 stays link-only and independent), so the lack-of-encryption case is still modelled. Open question for the lead: read it as a downgrade or drop it.

review_response.finding: Protection toggle does not test this threat (SDLS auth only, not confidentiality).
review_response.action: kept because the model has no confidentiality control. Coverage note records it: an 'on' result for TR45 means 'authentication does not stop interception', not a test of encryption.

review_response.finding: Single vector rf_link for a threat that spans any communication in the lifecycle.
review_response.action: fixed: added feeder_rf and user_terminal (basis weak, quote 'any communication/information in the satellite lifecycle'). Ground was not added: the key-compromise path is modelled by the credential on rf_link and ENISA names no ground action.

review_response.finding: Orphans and D-OTHER targets (PER-0004->TR52, PER-0005->TR35, LM-0007->TR37, EXF-0007->TR38).
review_response.action: kept; re-checked at the end. EX-0009*/EX-0008 moved from D-OTHER TR48 to D-UNDESCRIBED: ENISA's weak protocol is not a code defect.

review_response.finding: M2: feeder_rf and user_terminal weak vectors only produced structural differences
review_response.action: fixed: both removed; rf_link is the only vector; coverage note says the authentication controls do not stop interception.

review_response.finding: m1: EX-0006 kept circularly because other threats drop to TR45
review_response.action: kept on the ENISA text alone: 'Exploitation of weak communications protocols' read as protocol-level downgrade; drops of other threats are not a reason. Open question for the lead: re-point D-OTHER rows (TR13, TR29, TR33, TR38, TR39, TR44, TR47) to TR28/TR50 if the keep is withdrawn.

coverage_notes: The SDLS on/off switch tests authentication and anti-replay only; confidentiality is not a modelled control on the TT&C link, so EXF-0003 is accepted in every setting there. This is not a statement that the controls protect confidentiality.

DE-0011 (use of a compromised key) is modelled as a credential scenario but leads to no outcome beyond the passive capture, which does not depend on the key; the key clause is recorded and adds no result.
Feeder and user-terminal links are not mapped: ENISA says 'any communication' but names no link, and the model's capture result on them would not depend on the attacker's actions.
